five_full_records.Restrictions of Service: 988 crisis support is available by call or text and is described as free and confidential for residents in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, and Carroll County. No additional intake documents, referral-only restrictions, or eligibility requirements were stated in the available sources.

five_full_records.Description: A city-level behavioral health coordinating organization that operates a 988 crisis helpline for the region, runs a harm-reduction outreach team (Bmore POWER) offering on-the-ground outreach and overdose-harm-reduction services, and manages complaints and system navigation for behavioral-health providers in Baltimore City.
five_full_records.Reliability Description: Public review feedback is very limited; the available recent review expresses that the reviewer felt their concerns were ignored and reports distrust of health-care professionals, and the listing owner did not post a response. The organization’s official website and archival snapshots corroborate described programs (988 helpline, Bmore POWER outreach, complaint management), supporting the identity and stated activities. Because review text is sparse and skewed negative, user-experience claims should be treated cautiously and are not broadly generalizable.

five_full_records.Description: A Baltimore-based behavioral health provider offering multi-level addiction treatment and associated mental health care, including structured day programs, outpatient treatment, individual and group therapy, medication management, residential/housing support, and telehealth options.
five_full_records.Reliability Description: Google Maps reviews show a substantial set of first-hand client feedback: many reviewers praise caring, committed staff and describe effective PHP/IOP programming, on-site housing, and meals; recurring criticisms include staff turnover, small food portions, and delays or problems getting psychiatric medications. The organization’s verified website and Google Maps listing consistently describe a multi-level addiction-treatment continuum (PHP, IOP, outpatient), residential/housing services, medication management/psychiatry, and telehealth, which aligns with reviewer accounts. Newer reviews continue to show a mix of strong endorsements and sharp operational complaints, so public feedback is mixed but consistent with the services advertised.

five_full_records.Description: PEP (People Encouraging People) operates a physical recovery/behavioral health program that provides community-based rehabilitation and individualized support services for people with psychiatric or other disabling conditions; the organization’s website also states it is accredited by The Joint Commission.
five_full_records.Reliability Description: Recent reviewer comments are mixed: many people report helpful, caring, communicative staff who supported intake, housing assistance, or other services, while other reviewers describe serious safety and housing-related problems at some PEP sites, including allegations of unaddressed violence and pest issues. The most recent reviews include both brief positive reports and one detailed, severe complaint about a past site, so public feedback is currently mixed rather than uniformly positive or uniformly negative.
